scenes.title: The plan
scenes.vo: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.
scenes.cap: Here's the plan. First, the key ideas. Then, a worked example, step by step. Then, your checklist. And finally, a three-question quiz.

scenes.title: Key ideas
items: Multiples compare protocols; they don't set a "right" price.
scenes.vo: First, Fees: everything users pay. Revenue: the part that goes to the protocol or token holders (the rest goes to L.P.s/lenders). Earnings: revenue minus token incentives paid out. Next, Multiples: price-to-fees (P/F), price-to-sales (P/S, on revenue), price-to-earnings (P/E). Use F.D.V. as well as market cap, since unlocks will arrive (6.2). Then, Quality checks: is revenue growing without rising incentives? Is it concentrated in one pool or chain? Does it survive a bear market? Does the token actually receive it (value capture)? And finally, Multiples compare protocols; they don't set a "right" price.
scenes.cap: First, Fees: everything users pay. Revenue: the part that goes to the protocol or token holders (the rest goes to LPs/lenders). Earnings: revenue minus token incentives paid out. scenes.title: Worked example
steps: FDV $2B, annual revenue $100M, token incentives $60M → earnings $40M.
A rival with the same revenue but no incentives has earnings of $100M
scenes.vo: Let's work an example, step by step. F.D.V. $2B, annual revenue $100M, token incentives $60M to earnings $40M. P/S (F.D.V.) = 20 times ; P/E (F.D.V.) = 50 times . A rival with the same revenue but no incentives has earnings of $100M: at the same F.D.V. its P/E is 20 times . Same revenue, very different economics.
scenes.cap: Let's work an example, step by step. FDV $2B, annual revenue $100M, token incentives $60M → earnings $40M. P/S (FDV) = 20×; P/E (FDV) = 50×. A rival with the same revenue but no incentives has earnings of $100M: at the same FDV its P/E is 20×. Same revenue, very different economics.
